rejected.title: Solutions, solutes and solvents
card: A solution is a mixture in which one substance dissolves in another and spreads out evenly. You cannot see separate parts in it.
Solute
the substance that dissolves, such as salt in salty water.
Solvent
the substance that does the dissolving, such as the water in salty water.
Water dissolves so many substances, including some gases such as oxygen, that it is called the universal solvent. This does not mean it dissolves everything.
rejected.remember: Solute + solvent = solution. Water dissolves a lot, so it is the universal solvent.

a.q: Mia stirs sugar into hot tea until it disappears. Which part of this is the solute?
opts: The sugar
The tea
The sweet tea
The steam
a.why: The sugar dissolves and spreads out evenly, so it is the solute. The tea is the solvent because it does the dissolving, so calling it the solute reverses the two roles. The sweet tea is the whole solution.
a.clue: Which substance is the one that dissolves?

b.q: Liam stirs a spoon of salt into water and the salt disappears. A student says the water must be able to dissolve everything. Which reply is correct?
opts: Water dissolves many substances, but not all of them
Water dissolves every substance, so it is universal
Water dissolves only solids, such as salt and sugar
Only salt dissolves in water, not other substances
b.why: Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves so many substances, not all of them. The reply that water dissolves every substance misreads the name as meaning everything. Water also dissolves some gases, so it does not dissolve only solids.
b.clue: Think about what universal means in this name.

Solute
the substance that dissolves, such as salt in salty water.

version.remember: Solute + solvent = solution. Water dissolves a lot, so it is the universal solvent.

a.q: Ava stirs cordial powder into cold water until she can no longer see it. In this solution, which is the solvent?
opts: The water
The cordial powder
The finished cordial
The colour in the drink
a.why: The water does the dissolving, so it is the solvent. The powder is the solute, because it is the substance that dissolves, so picking it reverses the two roles. The finished cordial is the whole solution.
a.clue: Which substance dissolves the other one?

b.q: Noah reads that water is called the universal solvent. Which statement explains the name correctly?
opts: It dissolves a great many substances, though not all
It dissolves almost every solid, though not any gases
It is found in most places on Earth, so it is common
It dissolves every substance if stirred long enough
b.why: Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves so many substances, but it does not dissolve everything. It also dissolves some gases, such as oxygen, so the option about no gases is wrong. The name is about dissolving, not about where water is found.
b.clue: The name comes from what water does to other substances.

b.best: It dissolves a great many substances, though not all
